Lakers Nation > Blog > Lakers News > Lakers Injury Update: Luka Doncic Returns, Ziaire Williams Out Vs. Warriors Lakers News Lakers Injury Update: Luka Doncic Returns, Ziaire Williams Out Vs. Warriors
 Daniel Starkand Published: 10/30/2026 3 Min Read Oct 21, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts against the Golden State Warriors in the first half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images SHARE After missing Wednesday night’s win over the L.A. Clippers due to back tightness, Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is off the injury report and back in action on Friday night against the Golden State Warriors. It is the Lakers’ first group play game of the Emirates NBA Cup.
 Unfortunately though, the Lakers will be without starting forward Ziaire Williams for the second straight game due to left foot injury management. He was originally listed as questionable but then eventually ruled out, along with Cameron Carr (right oblique strain) and Adou Thiero (left knee injury management).
 Before the win over the Clippers, Lakers head coach JJ Redick did not seem concerned about Williams’ foot injury. It will be worth monitoring moving forward though after missing time in the preseason with the same issue.
 In Williams’ absence, the Lakers will likely turn to either Quentin Grimes or Jake LaRavia in the starting lineup. Grimes would make more sense as a point-of-attack defender who can help chase around Stephen Curry.
 Friday’s game is a rematch of Opening Night, when the Lakers pulled away in the second half to blow out the Warriors. Things got a bit chippy with Doncic and Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg doing some trash-talking during and after the game . he Lakers star got the better of Lendeborg in his NBA debut with the easy win.
 Lendeborg has already said he is looking forward to the rematch with Doncic , who undoubtedly is excited to get back on the court with the Golden State rookie after his comments last week.
 Luka Doncic still working to find rhythm
 Doncic is leading the NBA in scoring to begin the 2026-27 season and already has a 52-point game under his belt. But he still feels he is working to find his rhythm after taking so much time off in the offseason.
 “I’m still getting there honestly,” Doncic said of his rhythm. “This is the first time I didn’t play basketball in six or seven months, which is a long time. So, I’m not used to it. So, I think I’m still getting there. But you know, today was a little bit better.”
 Friday night would be the perfect time for Doncic to erupt offensively and lead the Lakers to another win.
